_about: Tested claim behind every study filed as Negative_result, and why it is or is not a no-effect edge on the pathway map. Edited by hand in the repo (not in Airtable). build_evidence_audit.py stops the deploy when a Negative_result study has no entry here, or when an entry names an edge that does not cite the study. Added 2026-10-15 after an external audit noted that five negative studies exist but no relation has the no-effect sign.

entries.tested_claim: Low-dose TORC1 inhibition with RTB101 reduces clinically symptomatic respiratory illness in adults aged 65 and older.
entries.model: Phase 2b and phase 3 randomised trials in older adults (phase 3 n=1024)
entries.endpoint: Clinically symptomatic respiratory illness (26% vs 25%, p=0.65 in phase 3); antiviral gene expression still rose.
entries.reason: Recorded as conflicting evidence on EVE-IMMUNE. A separate no-effect edge would misstate the tested link: the trial tested a drug (RTB101, not rapamycin-like) against a clinical outcome, not an interaction between two pathway nodes.

entries.tested_claim: Resveratrol, green tea extract, curcumin, oxaloacetic acid or medium-chain triglyceride oil extends lifespan in genetically heterogeneous mice.
entries.model: Mouse, genetically heterogeneous (Interventions Testing Program, three sites)
entries.reason: None of the tested compounds is a node of the pathway map, so there is no edge that could carry a no-effect sign.

entries.tested_claim: Resveratrol or simvastatin extends lifespan in genetically heterogeneous mice (negative arms of a study in which rapamycin extended lifespan).
entries.model: Mouse, genetically heterogeneous (Interventions Testing Program, three sites)
entries.reason: The negative arms concern compounds that are not nodes of the pathway map. The positive rapamycin arm of the same study is evidence for lifespan edges, not a null result.

entries.tested_claim: Four weeks of high-dose resveratrol improves insulin sensitivity, substrate metabolism or body composition in obese men.
entries.model: Humans, randomised placebo-controlled trial, obese men (n=24)
entries.endpoint: Insulin sensitivity, blood pressure, body composition
entries.reason: Resveratrol is not a node of the pathway map, and the tested link (compound to metabolic outcome in people) is not a step between two mapped nodes.

entries.tested_claim: Rapamycin co-exposure protects a mouse spermatogonial cell line (GC6-spg) from cisplatin-induced damage.
entries.model: GC6-spg spermatogonial cell line, in vitro
entries.reason: One cell line and a cell-damage endpoint, not a pathway step. It limits a protective claim made in female fertility models; it is not a tested-and-null pathway link.

entries.tested_claim: Long-term daily rapamycin causes hematological or clinical laboratory side effects in middle-aged common marmosets.
entries.model: Common marmoset (Callithrix jacchus), middle-aged, daily oral rapamycin for 9 months
entries.endpoint: Cellular blood counts and clinical laboratory markers: only minor changes in both sexes, although trough rapamycin levels were lower in females.
entries.reason: A tolerability result for a drug in one primate species, not a tested link between two mapped pathway nodes, so there is no edge that could carry a no-effect sign.

entries.tested_claim: Rapamycin slows epigenetic (DNA methylation) age in the blood of common marmosets.
entries.model: Common marmoset (Callithrix jacchus), whole-blood DNA methylation, rapamycin-treated cohort; clocks built with array data
entries.endpoint: Epigenetic age from marmoset clocks: no significant effect of rapamycin was detected.
entries.reason: A null result on one biomarker (blood DNA methylation age), not a pathway step. It does not show that rapamycin has no effect on aging in marmosets, only that these clocks did not register one, so it is not filed as a no-effect edge.
